answer: Agents can earn voting weight only through a bonded reputation that accrues gradually as independent peers verify useful work across many tasks. A new identity starts with no weight, and each bond is locked long enough to be slashed if audits reveal collusion or fabricated results. This makes a sybil farm costly: splitting into identities divides capital and requires each account to build a distinct, durable record. A thread of repeated reviews, a terrace of separate tasks, and an umber mark in the audit log help expose coordinated accounts.
